stimuli.description: Three distinct virtual reality environments: waterfront, urban, and green areas, each with three content variations (total 9 unique soundscape stimuli). Each stimulus was presented for 3 minutes.

tables.description: Pearson correlation coefficients between physical characteristics (LAeq, LCeq-Aeq, LA5-A95, Loudness, Sharpness, Green, Water, Sky, Grey, Luminance) and HRV indices (TP, SDNN, TSI).
Pearson correlation between psychological responses (PRSS domains, Soundscape quality, Overall preference) and HRV indices (TP, SDNN, TSI).
Differences in nodal efficiency for soundscape stimuli (Urban, Waterfront, Green) between restoration and non-restoration groups for various brain regions.
Demographic information and characteristics of participants including age, gender, PSS scores, noise sensitivity, TCI-RS scores, and WHOQOL-BREF scores.
Topographical map of Power Spectral Density (PSD) in the Alpha 1 band for restoration and non-restoration groups.
Acoustic and visual physical parameters for each soundscape site.

limitations: Adult participants may have preconceived notions about the characteristics of certain soundscapes based on prior experiences, and these preconceptions could potentially influence their emotional or physiological responses.
Challenges in applying the approach of this study, which is based on virtual environments, to real-life settings.
Challenges remain in selecting appropriate content based on the condition of each user or on time of day.
